title: Unveiling Compiler Faults via Attribute-Guided Compilation Space Exploration
problem: Compilers contain latent bugs that silently produce incorrect executable code, and existing random testing approaches lack systematic coverage of the vast space of compilation configurations and program attributes needed to trigger these faults.
motivation: Compiler correctness is foundational to software reliability; bugs in compilers propagate silently to all downstream software built with them.
method: The approach systematically explores the compiler configuration space using attribute-guided search, where program attributes (semantic properties, syntax patterns, input characteristics) guide test generation to maximize fault-triggering likelihood. Likely employs differential testing or output verification to detect generated incorrect code.
key_novelty: Attribute-guided exploration of compiler configuration space to systematically uncover compiler faults rather than relying on random or coverage-based testing.
contributions: Attribute-guided framework for compiler space exploration
Systematic methodology for triggering and detecting compiler bugs
limitations: Evaluation scope, specific baseline comparisons, and compiler targets not discussed in available title.
primary_theme: Compiler fault detection via systematic exploration
